_doc: Salt, potash, nitrate, sulfur, phosphate, lithium brine and bitumen-lake deposits; tonnes_ore is run-of-mine tonnage and ore_grade_kg_per_tonne the kilograms of product (salt, K2O-equivalent or P2O5-equivalent as noted per entry) per tonne. endowment is the total known resource, production to date plus remaining reserves (not only reserves, not oil or ore in place), to order of magnitude; where no defensible figure exists the key is omitted rather than guessed. conf: A = figure checked against a cited source in the audit, B = coordinate checked on Wikipedia and endowment approximate, C = from memory or a secondary summary. Entries with a status of modern are producing or recently producing; historic are worked out or pre-1800.

entries.name: Dead Sea brine
entries.source: Lake volume about 120 cubic kilometres at roughly 340 kg dissolved salts per cubic metre gives of order forty billion tonnes, a derivation not a source figure; coordinate approximate.
entries.contained_basis: Dissolved salts in the Dead Sea estimated at 44 billion tons by the Dead Sea Works; a popular-science source gives 37 billion tonnes, within 20%
entries.contained_source: Dead Sea Works description, https://wysinfo.com/?p=4603 : "The quantity of dissolved salts in the lake today is estimated at 44 billion tons"; BBC Science Focus, https://www.sciencefocus.com/planet-earth/how-much-salt-is-there-in-the-dead-sea : "about 37 billion tonnes"

entries.name: Wieliczka
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. No defensible endowment figure, omitted.
entries.contained_basis: About 25 million tonnes mined over the last 1,000 years; production only, a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Exciting Poland, Wieliczka, https://excitingpoland.com/?p=376 : "25 million tones of salt have been mined over the last 1,000 years"

entries.name: Hallstatt
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. No defensible endowment figure, omitted.
entries.contained_basis: Daily output about 1.5 t of salt (near-industrial scale from about 1200 BC) x 365 days x 850 years (assumption: working span from the German Wikipedia: Bronze Age mining from about 1500 BC to the 13th century BC debris flow, about 250 years, and Hallstatt-period mining from about 300 years later to the mid 4th century BC, about 600 years) = 465,000 t; medieval to modern working from 1311 not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: news.at, Hallstatt: Forscher stossen auf Komplex eisenzeitlicher Abbaukammern, https://www.news.at/technik/hallstatt-forscher-stossen-auf-komplex-eisenzeitlicher-abbaukammern : "Tagesproduktionen von etwa 1,5 Tonnen Salz"; German Wikipedia, Salzbergwerk Hallstatt, https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salzbergwerk_Hallstatt : first salt mining about 1500 BC, buried in the 13th century BC, resumed about 300 years later, stopped in the mid 4th century BC, first certain document 1311

entries.name: Khewra
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Wikipedia: reserve estimates range from 82 to over 600 million tons; geometric midpoint used.
entries.contained_basis: Wikipedia gives estimates of total reserves from 82 million tons to over 600 million tons; the upper figure is used, the lower is about 7 times less
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Khewra Salt Mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khewra_Salt_Mine : "Estimates of the total reserves of salt in the mines range from 82 million tons ... to over 600 million tons"

entries.name: Stassfurt (Zechstein rock salt)
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. No defensible endowment figure, omitted.
entries.contained_basis: No separate rock-salt tonnage: the only opened series, 'The Stassfurt Industry' (German Kali Works), gives crude salts (potash-bearing salts together) with no rock-salt split; tried: that series, German and English Wikipedia Stassfurt (dates only: systematic salt exploitation from 1856, no tonnage), a German Kalibergbau article (no Stassfurt tonnage); needs a rock-salt output table, for example Slotta, 150 Jahre Kaliproduktion in Deutschland, Kali und Steinsalz 3/2011, which did not open

entries.name: Great Salt Lake
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Dissolved salts of order five billion tonnes, from memory. The earlier entry was half a degree south of the lake centre.
entries.contained_basis: The lake holds over 4.5 billion tons of dissolved salt (Utah Geological Survey); industry removes about 2.5 Mt a year, not added
entries.contained_source: Utah Geological Survey, The Great Salt Lake (Public Information Series 8), https://ugspub.nr.utah.gov/publications/public_information/pi-8.pdf : "over 4.5 billion tons of salt"

entries.name: Salar de Uyuni
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Halite crust, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Salar de Uyuni estimated to contain 10 billion tonnes of salt, of which under 25,000 t a year is extracted
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Salar de Uyuni, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salar_de_Uyuni : "estimated to contain 10 billion tonnes ... of salt"

entries.name: Salar de Uyuni lithium
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Bolivian lithium resource of about 21 million tonnes (USGS), most of it at Uyuni; from memory.
entries.contained_basis: USGS lists Bolivian lithium resources at 23 Mt (2024); the row stands for the Uyuni salar, which holds most of the Bolivian resource (assumption); a resource figure with no production
entries.contained_source: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, Lithium, https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-lithium.pdf : "Resources are distributed as follows: Bolivia, 23 million tons" (2024)

entries.name: Qarhan Salt Lake (Qinghai)
entries.source: Coordinate from memory (the earlier entry at 37.5N 93.5E was about 1.5 degrees off); halite reserve of order fifty billion tonnes from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Qarhan Playa contains over 50 billion metric tons of salt (CNPC, per Wikipedia); a press report gives 55.5 billion tons of sodium chloride, an official-data report about 60 billion
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Qaidam Basin, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qaidam_Basin : "Qarhan Playa ... contains over 50 billion metric tons (55 billion short tons) of salt"

entries.name: Lake Assal
entries.source: Djibouti; coordinate from memory; no defensible endowment figure, omitted.
entries.contained_basis: Potential reserves assessed at 4 to 8 million tonnes; midpoint 6 Mt used
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Lake Assal (Djibouti), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Assal_(Djibouti) : "assessed with varying potential reserves of 4 to 8 million tonnes"

entries.name: Saskatchewan potash (Prairie Evaporite)
entries.source: Region centre approximate; reserves plus production of the order of twenty billion tonnes of ore, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Canadian potash reserves 1,100 Mt K2O equivalent (2023); assumes Saskatchewan holds nearly all of them (Prairie Evaporite, assumption); K2O basis, not KCl or ore; cumulative production since 1951 not added
entries.contained_source: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, Potash, https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-potash.pdf : reserves, Canada 1,100,000 thousand metric tons K2O equivalent

entries.name: Verkhnekamsk potash, Solikamsk
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Reserves of order ten billion tonnes of ore, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Russian potash reserves 650 Mt K2O equivalent (2023); assumes the Verkhnekamsk deposit holds most of them (assumption); K2O basis; production not added
entries.contained_source: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, Potash, https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-potash.pdf : reserves, Russia 650,000 thousand metric tons K2O equivalent

entries.name: Stassfurt potash
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. First industrial potash mine; no defensible endowment figure, omitted.
entries.contained_basis: Crude salts (potash-bearing salts, kainit and carnallite and the like, with associated salt; not K2O) raised by the Stassfurt industry 1861 to 1906, summed from the year-by-year table: 61.5 million t (2,293 t in 1861, 3,037,035 t in 1900, 5,311,903 t in 1906); production only, crude-salt tonnes not K2O, and the table does not split Stassfurt proper from the district's 45 mines, so the row stands for the district
entries.contained_source: The Stassfurt Industry, German Kali Works (New York, undated, data to 1906), https://distantreader.org/stacks/trust/uma/uma_ark+=13960=t0wq0q361.txt : table of crude salts production 1861 to 1906 in metric tons

entries.name: Boulby
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. No defensible endowment figure, omitted.
entries.contained_basis: Offshore polyhalite (a potassium-bearing mineral, not sylvinite) resources estimated at over a billion tonnes; potash production since 1973 not added
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Boulby Mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulby_Mine : "total resources estimated at over a billion tonnes" of polyhalite lying offshore

entries.name: Chilean nitrate belt (Maria Elena)
entries.source: Coordinate from memory (Maria Elena, Antofagasta region); sodium nitrate produced 1830-1930 of order seventy million tonnes, from memory. Replaces atacama_nitrate; tunupa_nitrate removed as unidentifiable.
entries.contained_basis: Sum of the 100 annual nitrate export figures 1830 to 1929 (860 t in 1830 to 2,898,141 t in 1929) = 82.1 Mt sodium nitrate exported; production only, so a lower bound (NaNO3 basis, not nitrogen basis)
entries.contained_source: Asociacion de Productores de Salitre en Chile, El Salitre: Historical Resume (Roberto Hernandez C., Valparaiso, 1930) as tabulated by Album del Desierto, Exports of Nitrate 1830 to 1929, https://albumdesierto.cl/ingles/2estadis.htm : annual 'Tons' table, e.g. 1830 860, 1890 1.065,277, 1929 2.898,141 (summed by script over all 100 rows)

entries.name: Sicilian sulfur belt
entries.source: Coordinate is Caltanissetta per Wikipedia; no defensible endowment figure, omitted.
entries.contained_basis: Sum of Italian sulfur output for each year 1900 to 1928 from the Bureau of Mines table = 10,614,296 long tons x 1.016 = 10.78 Mt; assumes Italian output was Sicilian (nearly all of it); 1700 to 1899 and after 1928 not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Frasch process, World Production of Sulphur 1900-1929 (US Bureau of Mines Information Circular 6329, 1930, p. 22), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frasch_process : Italy column, e.g. 1900 535,525; 1901 554,203; 1928 291,430 long tons

entries.name: Ijen
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Latitude sign corrected (the earlier entry was in the northern hemisphere, in the Pacific). No endowment figure.
entries.contained_basis: Miners extract 14 t a day x 365 days x 58 years (assumption: the row's first_worked of 1968 to 2026, taken from the existing row, not from the page) = 296,000 t; production only, and the page says this is about 20 percent of the continuous daily deposit
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Kawah Ijen, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawah_Ijen : miners "extract 14 tons per day"

entries.name: Gulf Coast salt-dome sulfur (Boling)
entries.source: Coordinate from memory (Boling dome, Texas); no defensible endowment figure, omitted.
entries.contained_basis: Boling dome Frasch sulfur: Texas Gulf more than 61,118,065 long tons + Duval 571,123 + Union 9,164 + Baker-Williams 1,435 = 61.70 million long tons x 1.016 t per long ton = 62.7 Mt; production only, a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Frasch process, table of Frasch mines, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frasch_process : Boling, Texas Gulf, ">61,118,065" long tons; Duval 571,123; Union 9,164; Baker-Williams 1,435

entries.name: Bone Valley (Florida)
entries.source: Coordinate from memory (Polk County); production plus reserves of order two billion tonnes of rock, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: United States phosphate rock reserves 1,000 Mt (2023, USGS); the Florida Bone Valley supplies the majority of US output, so this stands for it only roughly (assumption; Idaho, North Carolina and Utah are included); cumulative production since 1888 is not added
entries.contained_source: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, Phosphate Rock, https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-phosphate.pdf : reserves, United States 1,000,000 thousand metric tons; "Phosphate rock was produced in Florida, Idaho, North Carolina, and Utah"

entries.name: Khouribga (Ouled Abdoun)
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Morocco holds the largest reserves in the world (USGS); Ouled Abdoun share of order twenty billion tonnes, from memory. Replaces morocco_phosphate (0.9 degrees too far north).
entries.contained_basis: Ouled Abdoun basin, the Khouribga mine's basin, holds more than 26 billion tons (44% of Moroccan reserves); production since 1921 not added
entries.contained_source: Business Excellence / OCP, Phosphate forward sustainably: future-proofing Khouribga mine, https://bus-ex.com/article/phosphate-forward-sustainably-future-proofing-khouribga-mine : "Oulad Abdoun Basin, which comprises 44% of Morocco's phosphate reserves, more than 26 billion tons"

entries.name: Nauru
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Exhausted island deposit, order a hundred million tonnes produced, from memory. nauru_second_phosphate removed as a duplicate.
entries.contained_basis: About 43 million tons produced since independence in 1968; mining from 1906 to 1968 is not added, so a lower bound; the island's phosphate was largely exhausted in the 1990s
entries.contained_source: WorldAtlas, How Has Phosphate Mining in Nauru Led to an Environmental Catastrophe, https://www.worldatlas.com/articles/how-phosphate-mining-in-nauru-has-led-to-an-environmental-catastrophe.html : "Since independence, the country has produced approximately 43 million tons of phosphate"
